name: Ben's Chili Bowl
tagline: The half-smoke that has held down U Street since 1958.
description: Ben and Virginia Ali opened on U Street in 1958 and stayed open through the 1968 uprising, the Metro construction years and everything since. The chili half-smoke is the order; the counter is the landmark.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on the restaurant's own locations page; Yelp updated 2026-08. Open since 1958. The first DC row and a clean one — as expected for a landmark, and consistent with the LA finding that recall quality tracks how well documented a business is.

name: Ben's Next Door
tagline: The Ali family's full-service dining room beside the original.
description: A sit-down restaurant and bar next to Ben's Chili Bowl, built by the same family for people who want the U Street tradition with table service, cocktails and a longer menu.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own site; Yelp updated 2026-08. Sits directly beside Ben's Chili Bowl at 1213 — two adjacent street numbers, same block, different businesses. Worth noting for the shared-address rule: these are near-neighbours, not co-tenants, and no rule fires.

name: Oohh's & Aahh's
tagline: U Street soul food, portioned for people who are hungry.
description: A narrow U Street kitchen turning out salmon cakes, smothered chicken, mac and cheese and candied yams. The line out the door on a weekend night is the review.

_verified.note: Address and ZIP on the row confirmed exactly; phone and first-party domain added; Yelp current to August 2026. FOUNDED YEAR CORRECTED 2001 → 2003. The business's own About page says it started in 2003 as a carryout on U Street; the 2001 already on the row had no source behind it. MULTI-LOCATION: the brand now runs several locations and the site has a locations page. This row is the U STREET original only — the slug is generic (`oohhs-and-aahhs`) rather than location-scoped, so if you ever add a sibling location it will need renaming first. Ownership carried by first-party material and Food Network coverage; the founders are two brothers cooking their grandmothers' recipes.

name: Florida Avenue Grill
tagline: The world's oldest soul food restaurant, open since 1944.
description: Lacey Wilson opened the Grill in 1944 and it has been serving scrapple, grits, half-smokes and pork chops from the same counter ever since. Photographs of eight decades of customers cover the walls.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own site. Open since 1944 and billed as the oldest soul food restaurant in the world. Note the site is http, not https — recorded as found rather than silently upgraded, since guessing a scheme is the same class of error as guessing a domain.

name: Henry's Soul Cafe
tagline: Sweet potato pie and soul food takeout on U Street since 1968.
description: Henry's is a takeout window with a reputation built almost entirely on its sweet potato pie, plus ribs, fried chicken and greens. A U Street constant through every wave of change on the corridor.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on the chain's own U Street location page; Yelp updated 2026-06. Founded 1968 by Henry E. Smith. A second location exists in Oxon Hill, MD — out of scope for this city corpus, but a candidate row if the founder ever adds a DMV-metro tier.

name: Fish in the Hood
tagline: Fried whiting, catfish and jumbo shrimp on upper Georgia Avenue.
description: A Petworth-area fish counter frying to order — whiting, catfish, wings — with hot sauce and half-and-half bread. Cash-and-carry, no pretense, consistently good.

_verified.note: Both address fields were wrong: drafted 4801 Georgia Ave NW / 20011, actual 3601 Georgia Ave NW / 20010. Twelve hundred blocks apart puts it in a different neighbourhood — Park View, not Petworth — so this is a geocode that would have succeeded and landed a mile off, the same failure class as Vicky's All Day in LA. Two more things for the founder: Yelp now lists the business as 'Fish in the Neighborhood' while its own material still says 'Fish in the Hood', so the name may want a review-sheet decision; and no real website exists — only a dormant Blogspot and a NetWaiter ordering page — hence the checked null. Cash only.

name: Puddin'
tagline: Louisiana comfort food and bread pudding at Union Market.
description: Toyin Alli brought her Louisiana grandmother's recipes to Union Market — gumbo, jambalaya, red beans, and the bread pudding the stall is named for.

_verified.note: Address confirmed by the Union Market landlord's own tenant directory; Yelp updated 2026-08. Founded by Toyin Alli, grown from an Eastern Market street stall. website_url is a deliberate null: the only URLs that surfaced were a Menufy ordering page and aggregator listings, and a directory that links a business to a third-party order host has misrepresented whose page it is. Founder can supply the real one at review.

name: Cane
tagline: Trinidadian cooking on H Street from chef Peter Prime.
description: Peter Prime and Jeanine Prime built a small H Street dining room around Trinidadian food — doubles, curry goat, jerk chicken, pholourie — and earned national attention for it without changing the scale.

_verified.note: Address confirmed by the Michelin Guide entry and Yelp, updated 2026-08. Michelin Bib Gourmand. website_url is a checked null — the ordering link is a Toast page, not the restaurant's own domain, and the same reasoning as Puddin' applies. Note 403 H St NE and Ethiopic at 401 H St NE are adjacent street numbers, not a shared address.

name: St. James
tagline: Caribbean fine dining on 14th Street.
description: A 14th Street dining room bringing Trinidadian and wider Caribbean cooking to a full tasting-menu setting, with a bar program to match.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own site; Yelp updated 2026-07. Opened May 2022, owned by Jeanine Prime. Trades as 'St. James – Modern Caribbean'; the corpus name is the short form, which is fine, but flag it if the founder wants listing names to match signage.

name: Turning Natural
tagline: Juice bar putting fresh produce in the wards that lack it.
description: Jerri Evans built Turning Natural into a juice and smoothie chain deliberately sited east of the river and in neighborhoods underserved by grocery stores. Cold-pressed juice, smoothies, and a health mission that is explicit rather than decorative.
address_line_1: 2025 Martin Luther King Jr Ave SE

_verified.note: Not a relocation and not an entity mismatch — a wrong street on the right business. The drafted 3220 Pennsylvania Ave SE appears nowhere on the company's own locations page, which lists Anacostia (2025 Martin Luther King Jr Ave SE), Capitol Hill (750 C St SE), 6833 4th St NW, and Lanham MD. The drafted ZIP 20020 is Anacostia's, not Capitol Hill's, so the row was always aiming at the Anacostia flagship and only the street line was wrong; corrected to match. Founded by Jerri Evans. phone is a checked null — no number surfaced on the company's own site or the review source, and inventing one for a juice bar people actually call is the failure this pass exists to prevent. Worth flagging to the founder that Turning Natural has three other DC locations that could each be their own row.

name: Roaming Rooster
tagline: Fried chicken sandwiches that started from a food truck.
description: The Habtemariam family started with one truck and grew Roaming Rooster into a multi-location fried chicken operation, built on a sandwich that DC lines up for.

_verified.note: Address, ZIP and first-party domain on the row confirmed; phone added; Yelp current to June 2026. Ownership is well sourced — the Washington Informer names it one of two Black-owned restaurants in Western Market's first phase, and the founding family is named across coverage. MULTI-LOCATION: this address is the Western Market stall in Foggy Bottom; the brand also operates on Bladensburg Rd, U St and Wisconsin Ave. Same generic-slug caution as Oohh's & Aahh's.

name: Dogon
tagline: Chef Kwame Onwuachi's Afro-Caribbean restaurant in Southwest.
description: Named for the Dogon people and built around the Afro-Caribbean and West African threads in Onwuachi's cooking, Dogon is his return to DC dining after Kith/Kin — ambitious, plated, and rooted in a specific history.

_verified.note: Address confirmed by the Michelin Guide and Yelp, updated 2026-07. Chef Kwame Onwuachi's Afro-Caribbean restaurant, named for the Dogon people of Mali. Two things the founder should know. It sits inside the Salamander Hotel, so the street address resolves to the hotel — the geocode will be right but the pin lands on a hotel entrance, which is worth a line in the listing description rather than a data fix. And the phone is a toll-free 844 number, i.e. the hotel's reservations line, not a direct restaurant number; recorded as found because it is the number a customer would actually be given. website_url left null: the restaurant's page lives under the hotel's domain and linking a listing to a hotel homepage misrepresents where it points.

name: Keren Restaurant
tagline: Eritrean breakfast and coffee ceremony near Adams Morgan.
description: A small Eritrean restaurant known for ful, shiro and a morning crowd that treats it as a community fixture. Traditional coffee service, and a room where regulars linger.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own site; Yelp updated 2026-08. Open since 1987, just south of Adams Morgan. One correction for the founder rather than for the data: Keren is Eritrean, and several aggregators — including Yelp — file it as Ethiopian. If the corpus row carries an Ethiopian category or description, it should say Eritrean; the two are distinct cuisines and a directory serving these communities is the last place that should blur them. Trades as 'Keren Cafe & Restaurant'.

name: Dukem Ethiopian Restaurant
tagline: Little Ethiopia's U Street anchor, with live music most weekends.
description: One of the restaurants that made the U Street corridor synonymous with Ethiopian food in DC. Full injera platters, tej, and live traditional music on the weekend.

_verified.note: Phone and first-party domain added; ZIP 20009 and founding year 1997 on the row both confirmed; Yelp current to August 2026. ADDRESS NOTE: sources render this as 1114-1118 U St NW, a double storefront. The row keeps the single 1114 because a hyphenated range geocodes unreliably — the pin lands correctly either way. OWNERSHIP TIER, worth your tick: the sources establish an Ethiopian-founded family restaurant operating since 1997, but none of them states Black ownership in those words. Cuisine is not evidence of ownership and I did not treat it as such — this is an inference-adjacent row and the weakest ownership record of the thirteen.

name: Chercher Ethiopian Restaurant
tagline: Shaw Ethiopian kitchen with a deep vegetarian platter.
description: Named for the Chercher mountains, this Shaw restaurant is a reliable stop for vegetarian combinations, kitfo and a room that stays busy without being loud.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own site; Yelp updated 2026-08. Named for the Chercher highlands in eastern Ethiopia. Full trading name is 'Chercher Ethiopian Restaurant & Mart' — it runs a grocery alongside the restaurant, which the corpus name drops. Two live domains surfaced (chercherrestaurant.com and chercherdc.com); recorded the one the restaurant's own pages link as canonical rather than guessing between them.

name: Letena
tagline: Fast-casual Ethiopian in Columbia Heights.
description: Letena reworked Ethiopian food into a build-your-own counter format without losing the cooking — shiro, gomen, doro wat, all made properly and served fast.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own site; Yelp updated 2026-08. Family-owned, in the Washingtonian 100 Very Best Restaurants 2025. Suite 121 added — 3100 14th St NW is the DC USA retail complex, and without the suite the geocoder resolves to the complex rather than the restaurant, the same failure the Leimert Park and Baldwin Hills rows had in LA. One thing to fix at review: social_instagram is holding a Facebook URL because no Instagram handle surfaced. That is the wrong field for it, and rather than invent a handle I have put the sourced link where the founder will see it — either the corpus needs a social_facebook field or this should be nulled.

name: Ethiopic
tagline: H Street Ethiopian dining with a full bar.
description: A more polished take on Ethiopian dining on H Street — the same traditional platters, served in a room designed for a long dinner rather than a quick one.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on the restaurant's own hours-and-location page; Yelp updated 2026-07. Clean row — own domain, own Instagram, both first-party. Note the adjacency already flagged on Cane: 401 and 403 H St NE are neighbouring storefronts, not a shared address, so the Phase 2d duplicate rule does not fire.

name: Appioo African Bar & Grill
tagline: Ghanaian cooking and live music in Shaw.
description: Chef Prince Matey's Shaw restaurant serves jollof, waakye, goat light soup and grilled tilapia, with West African music and a room that turns celebratory late.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own hours page; Yelp updated 2026-06. Ghanaian home cooking with live music on weekends. Site is http, recorded as found for the same reason as Florida Avenue Grill — guessing a scheme is guessing. Also independently listed as Black-owned on EatOkra, which is a useful corroboration for the ownership_label rather than for the address.

name: Bukom Cafe
tagline: Adams Morgan West African kitchen and late-night music room.
description: A long-running Adams Morgan spot for Ghanaian and West African cooking with live highlife and reggae, where the kitchen stays open later than most of the block.

_verified.note: The clearest argument in this whole pass for checking twice. The first search surfaced a November 2025 PoPville piece headlined 'Is Bukom Cafe no more?' — sporadic hours, the space being cleaned out, an Instagram dormant since February. Writing `closed` off that headline would have deleted a business that is trading today: PoPville reported in December 2025 that it was reopening, and Yelp updated 2026-07 shows it operating with a new menu and full hours. Open in Adams Morgan since 1992, named for Bukom Square in Accra. website_url is a null on purpose — three candidate domains surfaced and none is unambiguously the current one, and picking wrong sends users to a stale or squatted page. Founder should confirm at review.

name: Open Crumb
tagline: West African scratch cooking on H Street NE.
description: Chef Peter Opare's scratch kitchen built a following in Anacostia before moving to H Street NE, serving West African staples — jollof, egusi, grilled tilapia, plantain — cooked to order rather than held on a steam table. The menu is short and rotates, and the counter service is quick enough for a weekday lunch.

_verified.note: Clean confirmation, no change needed. Address, ZIP, phone and first-party domain on the row all match; Yelp current to June 2026. RELOCATION ALREADY REFLECTED: the business moved from Anacostia to H Street NE, and the 822 H St NE on the row is the current address, not the old one — worth recording because a stale Anacostia address is exactly the failure this pass exists to catch. Ownership rests on the restaurant's own framing as serving West African food and the wider Black diaspora plus local food-press coverage; editorial tier, not a first-party ownership statement.

name: Player's Lounge
tagline: Ward 8 neighborhood bar and kitchen, a Congress Heights fixture.
description: A Martin Luther King Jr Avenue bar and restaurant that has anchored Ward 8 nightlife for years — wings, fish, drinks, and a room where the neighborhood actually knows each other.
address_line_1: 2737 Martin Luther King Jr Ave SE

_verified.note: Address and ZIP on the row confirmed exactly; phone added; Yelp current to August 2026, so this Anacostia institution is trading. NO WEBSITE — the business runs on Facebook, and a Facebook page is not a website under our own rule, so `website_url` stays null rather than pointing at a social profile. The order.online link is a third-party ordering host and likewise not a website; it is cited here only as evidence the business is live.

name: Sankofa Video Books & Cafe
tagline: Haile Gerima's bookstore, café and film archive near Howard.
description: Filmmaker Haile Gerima and Shirikiana Gerima built Sankofa into a bookstore, café and Pan-African film archive across from Howard University — a place that has hosted organizing meetings as often as book signings since 1998.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own site; Yelp updated 2026-07. Founded by filmmakers Haile Gerima and Shirikiana Aina, across from Howard. Worth noting against the NuVegan row: Sankofa sits on the same Georgia Ave corridor a few blocks north and is trading normally, so that closure was a single storefront changing hands, not a corridor in decline.

name: Loyalty Bookstores
tagline: Petworth bookstore built around writers of color and queer writers.
description: Hannah Oliver Depp's shop stocks with intent — writers of color, queer writers, and translated work — and runs a reading and event program that has made it a hub well beyond Petworth.

_verified.note: Moved. The store's own /move page says the last full day at 843 Upshur St NW was Sunday, February 2nd, and it is now at 4203 9th St NW — around the corner, still Petworth, still 20011. The page does not state the year, which is worth recording honestly: the move is first-party sourced and the new address is current, but the date is not, so do not repeat a year we cannot show. Founded 2019 by Hannah Oliver Depp. A Silver Spring MD location also exists and is out of scope for the DC corpus. Third relocation in this pass and the first one where the ZIP survived the move, which is exactly why ZIP-matching alone would not have caught it.

name: Nubian Hueman
tagline: Anacostia lifestyle boutique carrying independent Black designers.
description: Anika Hobbs curates apparel, jewelry, art and home goods from Black designers across the diaspora, in a storefront inside the Anacostia Arts Center that doubles as a community gathering space.

_verified.note: Trading; Yelp updated 2026-06 and the Anacostia BID was running a Nubian Hueman programme this month. Founded by Anika Hobbs, inside the Anacostia Arts Center. This is a co-tenant row, not a duplicate — see the shared-address note on anacostia-arts-center. STREET RENAME, 2026-08-14: the address on this row read "Good Hope Rd SE". D.C. Law 25-46, the Marion Barry Avenue Designation Act of 2023, renamed that stretch to Marion Barry Ave SE; the new signs went up 2023-11-18. Nominatim resolves the Marion Barry form at this house number and returns nothing for the Good Hope form, so the old name was silently costing this row its map pin. Many businesses still print the old name on their own sites — that is a display choice, not the legal address, and the corpus carries the current one.

name: Anacostia Arts Center
tagline: Ward 8 arts hub housing galleries, small businesses and a black box theater.
description: A Good Hope Road building converted into gallery space, a black box theater and small retail bays — the physical center of gravity for arts east of the Anacostia River.

_verified.note: Open; Yelp updated 2026-05. 9,300 sq ft with a black box theater, gallery, lounge and several small businesses. Worth recording what this address now looks like after the MahoganyBooks removal: the corpus had three rows here, and it now has two — this building and Nubian Hueman, one arts-culture and one retail. That is precisely the co-tenant shape the Phase 2d rule was relaxed for, so the dry run should emit a `shared-address` warning for founder confirmation and not a hard failure. The building's own phone and the tenant's own phone are different numbers, which is the corroboration that these are two entities rather than one row entered twice. STREET RENAME, 2026-08-14: the address on this row read "Good Hope Rd SE". D.C. Law 25-46, the Marion Barry Avenue Designation Act of 2023, renamed that stretch to Marion Barry Ave SE; the new signs went up 2023-11-18. Nominatim resolves the Marion Barry form at this house number and returns nothing for the Good Hope form, so the old name was silently costing this row its map pin. Many businesses still print the old name on their own sites — that is a display choice, not the legal address, and the corpus carries the current one.

name: Anacostia Playhouse
tagline: Ward 8 theater producing new work and community programming.
description: A working theater east of the river staging new plays, youth programs and community events, in a neighborhood the city's arts funding has historically skipped.

_verified.note: Address confirmed on its own about page; Yelp updated 2026-01 and TheatreWashington still lists it as an active venue. Clean row.

name: Honfleur Gallery
tagline: Anacostia contemporary art gallery on Good Hope Road.
description: A contemporary gallery in Historic Anacostia showing emerging and mid-career artists, with a program deliberately built around artists of color and the neighborhood around it.

_verified.note: Open; Yelp updated 2026-02, and the gallery's own site is taking tour bookings. Contemporary art space in Historic Anacostia, run by ARCH Development Corporation. Sources disagree on the hours — Tue–Sat noon–5 in one place, Thu–Sat plus by-appointment in another — which is a reminder that hours are the fastest-rotting field in any directory and should not be drafted from a search at all; the corpus does not carry them and should not start. Note this is 1241 Good Hope Rd SE, next door to 1231 and not the same building, so it is not part of the Anacostia Arts Center shared-address cluster. Last unverified DC row: the DC pass is now complete at 27 of 27. STREET RENAME, 2026-08-14: the address on this row read "Good Hope Rd SE". D.C. Law 25-46, the Marion Barry Avenue Designation Act of 2023, renamed that stretch to Marion Barry Ave SE; the new signs went up 2023-11-18. Nominatim resolves the Marion Barry form at this house number and returns nothing for the Good Hope form, so the old name was silently costing this row its map pin. Many businesses still print the old name on their own sites — that is a display choice, not the legal address, and the corpus carries the current one.

name: Step Afrika!
tagline: The first professional company dedicated to stepping.
description: C. Brian Williams founded Step Afrika! in 1994 as the world's first professional company built around stepping, tracing the form from African American fraternities and sororities back to South African gumboot dance. Now one of DC's largest African American performing arts organizations.

_verified.note: Confirmed at 1333 H St NE; Yelp updated 2026-06. One thing for the founder rather than for the data: every source records this address as c/o the Atlas Performing Arts Center, because Step Afrika! is a touring dance company headquartered in the Atlas rather than a venue a visitor drops into. The address is right and the pin will land right, but a user tapping this expecting a storefront will find a theater box office, so the listing description should say 'company offices at the Atlas Performing Arts Center' — the same class of note as Dōgon inside the Salamander. Founded 1994 by C. Brian Williams; the first professional company in the world dedicated to stepping.

name: District of Clothing
tagline: DC apparel brand printing purpose-driven messages.
description: Danielle Vincent left a government job to build District of Clothing, an apparel line whose graphics carry explicit messages about purpose, equity and the city itself.

_verified.note: Ownership is strong — the founder is named across NBC4, Bustle, Black Enterprise, Forbes and the Washington Informer, and the 2014 founding year on the row is confirmed. NO SHOP URL was returned as a real link by any source. The founder's personal site came back as a real URL but that is a different property, so `website_url` stays null rather than being pattern-guessed from the brand name. MINOR TYPE QUESTION: the row is `hybrid`; coverage describes the brand as deliberately online-only, which would make `virtual` more accurate. Left unchanged because both types geocode as skip-online and neither affects the gate — flagging it rather than churning the row.

name: BloomBars
tagline: Columbia Heights arts space where nobody pays at the door.
description: A donation-based community arts venue on 11th Street NW running live music, open mics, poetry and children's programming — deliberately free at the point of entry so the arts stay reachable in a rapidly changing neighbourhood.

_verified.note: Address, phone and first-party domain confirmed together. Founded by John Chambers; a long-running Black-led Columbia Heights arts nonprofit.

name: Skin Beauty Bar
tagline: Capitol Hill skincare studio focused on darker skin tones.
description: A Barracks Row skincare studio on the second floor of 8th Street SE, doing facials, chemical peels and treatment plans built for melanin-rich skin rather than adapted to it after the fact.

_verified.note: Address (2nd floor) and phone confirmed. NO WEBSITE was returned by either source — left null rather than guessed at a plausible domain. Ownership is sourced to an Essence feature on Black-owned DC spas, which is editorial rather than first-party.

name: Paris Alexander Day Spa
tagline: Dupont-area day spa, three decades on R Street.
description: A full-service day spa just off 17th Street doing massage, facials and body treatments — long enough established on R Street NW to have outlasted most of the block around it.

_verified.note: Address with suite number and phone confirmed; suite is load-bearing for geocoding. NO WEBSITE returned — left null. Ownership sourced to the same Essence feature; editorial, not first-party.

name: The LAB Fitness DC
tagline: Mount Vernon Triangle gym built around small-group coaching.
description: A downtown training studio running small-group strength and conditioning rather than machine-lined open floor — coached sessions where the person leading knows your name and your last set.

_verified.note: Address and first-party domain confirmed. TWO THINGS FOR THE FOUNDER: (1) the listed phone carries a 361 area code, which is Corpus Christi TX, not DC — plausible for an owner-carried mobile but worth one call to confirm before publish. (2) Ownership is sourced to buyblack.org, a peer Black-owned-business directory, which is the weakest tier of ownership evidence we accept. Both are verify-before-publish items, not blockers on the record itself.

name: BOOMBOX Boxing Club
tagline: Navy Yard boxing gym — bags, rounds and no mirrors.
description: A boxing club off Van Street doing group rounds, bagwork and one-on-one coaching, built for people who want to actually learn to box rather than take a boxing-themed cardio class.

_verified.note: Address with suite, phone and first-party domain all confirmed together; the suite number is load-bearing for geocoding in Navy Yard, where 1221 Van St is a multi-tenant building. Ownership sourced to an Essence feature on Black-owned fitness studios — editorial rather than first-party, same tier as the Skin Beauty Bar and Paris Alexander rows.

name: CitySwing
tagline: DC's first indoor golf studio, downtown at Mount Vernon.
description: An indoor golf studio on New York Avenue running simulator bays, lessons and clinics — built deliberately to open golf up to people the sport has historically priced and postured out.

_verified.note: Address, phone and first-party domain confirmed together. Ownership is well sourced — African American Golfer's Digest covered the opening as a named Black-woman-founded business. NOTE ON PROVENANCE: my own search query carried a wrong owner name from recall; the sources corrected it. No owner name is stored on the row, and none should be inferred from this note.

name: Black Bella Spa & Wellness
tagline: Congress Heights spa blending Eastern technique and Western tech.
description: A spa and wellness studio inside the Sycamore & Oak retail village, offering massage, lymphatic work and esthetics — clinical training applied in a neighbourhood that has had almost none of it.

_verified.note: ADDRESS CORRECTED AT DRAFT TIME: roundup coverage gives the village as 1100 Oak Dr SE; the tenant-level sources give 1110 Oak Dr SE with ZIP 20032. Took the tenant-level number. NO PHONE and no unit number were returned — both left null rather than guessed. Ownership sourcing here is the strongest tier in this batch: Sycamore & Oak is a purpose-built Black-owned retail village, documented by the Mayor's office, Black Enterprise, the AFRO and PR Newswire, and this business has its own first-party tenant page.

name: WeFitDC
tagline: Congress Heights gym built around whole-body community wellness.
description: A coached fitness studio in the Sycamore & Oak village doing personal training and group work, with a whole-body framing that treats fitness as health rather than aesthetics.

_verified.note: Unit 2 is sourced, not inferred, and is load-bearing for geocoding a 14-tenant retail village. NO PHONE returned — left null. Ownership carried by the Sycamore & Oak village documentation plus a first-party tenant page. Fresha is a booking host, not a website, and is cited only as the source of the unit number.

name: Sweet Tooth Cafe & Cakes
tagline: Anacostia bakery and halal comfort kitchen on MLK Ave.
description: A Martin Luther King Jr Avenue bakery doing gourmet desserts and halal comfort food — one of the Ward 8 storefronts the city has spotlit as new Black-owned business on the corridor.
address_line_1: 2323 Martin Luther King Jr Ave SE

_verified.note: HELD AS DRAFT, NOT PUBLISHED. The business's own site states the Anacostia location is temporarily closed, so publishing it would put a shut door in front of a user. The record is sound — address, ZIP, phone and first-party domain all confirmed, and ownership is sourced to a DC Deputy Mayor release specifically celebrating new Black-owned Ward 8 businesses, which is a first-tier source. Publish from the review sheet when it reopens. Separately: a different, unrelated "Sweet Tooth" at 1219 Connecticut Ave NW shows CLOSED on Yelp — not this business, and not drafted.

name: SWEAT DC
tagline: Park View strength studio — coached, loud, nobody judged.
description: A Georgia Avenue strength and group fitness studio built on science-backed programming and real coaching, run on a stated premise that everyone is welcome and nobody is watched.

_verified.note: MULTI-LOCATION: SWEAT runs four DC studios — Park View, H Street (501 H St NE), West End (1108 24th St NW) and Shaw (1818 7th St NW). This row is PARK VIEW ONLY, chosen because it is the one location where address, suite, ZIP and phone were all sourced together, and its Yelp page is current to August 2026. The slug is deliberately location-scoped so the other three can be added as sibling rows without a collision — founder call whether to add them. Ownership sourced to an InsideHook interview with the founder plus the studio's own site.

name: Chris Pyrate & Friends
tagline: Art-first streetwear from a DC-born illustrator.
description: A streetwear label built out of Chris Pyrate's illustration work — signature patterns and characters carried onto clothing, sold from the artist's own storefront in the Sycamore & Oak village.

_verified.note: First-party tenant page and Instagram handle both confirmed as real URLs rather than pattern-guessed. NO PHONE returned — left null. Ownership carried by the AFRO's tenant interviews plus the village's own documentation; the artist is named DC-born in every source. Shares 1110 Oak Dr SE with Black Bella (beauty-grooming) and WeFitDC (wellness-health) — different categories, so this reads as a `shared-address` warning, not a duplicate.

name: Soufside Creative
tagline: Congress Heights Art & Culture Center outpost, east of the river.
description: The Congress Heights Art & Culture Center's storefront in the Sycamore & Oak village — exhibition and creative space keeping Ward 8 art on Ward 8 ground rather than downtown.

_verified.note: THINNEST ROW IN THIS BATCH, and deliberately so. Address and ZIP are sourced through the village; ownership is sourced three ways (technical.ly, Black Enterprise, AFRO all state every Sycamore & Oak tenant is Black-owned). But NO PHONE and NO FIRST-PARTY URL were returned. The other tenants' sycamoreandoak.com pages came back as real URLs in search results; this one did not, so I did NOT construct one from the pattern — a guessed URL that 404s is worse than no URL. Founder: one look at the village directory fills both fields.
